reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the mechanical and corrosion properties of the amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film and the role of its homogeneous amorphous structure, but provides no data on high-temperature oxidation resistance or on the detrimental effect of phase segregation, leaving two key premises unsupported.
premises: Amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film exhibits high compressive strength (3.6 GPa) and deformability (58%)
Amorphous AlTiVNb HEA film shows corrosion resistance comparable to 316L stainless steel in 3.5% NaCl
High strength is attributed to disordered state, nanostructure, and lattice distortion
Corrosion resistance is attributed to chemical disorder, cocktail effect, and homogeneous amorphous structure
Phase segregation or partial crystallization will compromise strength, corrosion, and oxidation resistance
